problem: Removing the time-went-backwards check means an earlier `now` is appended behind a later one (line 35), and eviction from the front of the deque (lines 27-28) then goes wrong: requests over the limit are allowed after a backward step, and expired entries keep counting and cause wrong refusals.

With timestamps out of order, `q[0]` is no longer the oldest entry or may be in the future, so `retry_after` returns wrong values, including waits longer than the window (e.g. 110.0 for a 10s window).
The branch removes documented behaviour (ValueError on non-monotonic time) and adds no tests, so neither the removal nor the new out-of-order behaviour is covered.
`_last_now` is still written in `_observe` on every call but never read, which makes it look as if time ordering is still enforced.
Already on main: a deque is created for every key and never removed once empty, so keys chosen by clients can grow `_accepted` without limit.
Already on main: `now` is never validated, so a NaN timestamp is stored and never evicted (`nan <= cutoff` is always False), locking the key out permanently and making `retry_after` return nan.
